November 27, 2026


# Grifols acquires Biotest’s plasma collection centers for €220M to streamline plasma sourcing in Europe


[Download PDF](https://www.grifols.com/documents/6155538/8988583/np-20261127-en.pdf/b4a6f80d-803f-d3c6-2b0b-c9240ab54a3f?t=1795772195999)


**- The acquisition supports Grifols’ broader strategy to strengthen regional plasma sourcing and contribute to Europe’s long-term plasma self-sufficiency, through more efficient management of existing collection network - Under a 30-year plasma supply agreement, Grifols will supply Biotest with plasma, supporting long-term supply continuity for its manufacturing operations - The transaction also includes all Biotest’s European third-party plasma supply agreements, allowing Grifols to optimize plasma sourcing and capture efficiencies in procurement and supply chain management - The operation will allow Biotest’s 47 plasma donation centers to be integrated into Grifols’ existing European network, bringing the combined network to 97 sites across Germany, Austria, Hungary and the Czech Republic, under a single operating model that will enable more coordinated management of plasma collection across Europe - The consideration will be settled by offsetting against Biotest debt owed to Grifols**


***Barcelona, Spain, November 27, 2026*** ***–*** Grifols (MCE:GRF, MCE:GRF.P, NASDAQ:GRFS), a global healthcare company and leading producer of plasma-derived medicines, has announced that it has acquired Biotest’s European plasma collection business for €220 million by its subsidiary Grifols Worldwide Operations Ltd. The acquisition includes 14 collection centers in Germany, 19 in Hungary and 14 in the Czech Republic, consolidating management of Grifols’ European collection network. The transaction also includes Biotest’s European plasma supply contracts with third parties. This will allow the company to adjust its sourcing mix as production requirements change, coordinate procurement and logistics across the entire network, and streamline its engagement with regulatory authorities across European markets.


The operation will allow Biotest’s 47 plasma donation centers to be integrated into Grifols’ existing European network, bringing the combined network to 97 sites across Germany, Austria, Hungary and the Czech Republic. Through the integration of Biotest’s plasma collection operations, Grifols expects to capture efficiencies by sharing operational best practices across its European network, adopting a more consistent approach to staffing, procurement and supply chain management, as well as optimizing its network of donation centers to improve collection productivity and optimize plasma cost per liter.


Grifols will manage plasma supply through two complementary agreements. Under a 30-year agreement, the company will supply Biotest with plasma, supporting greater predictability in plasma collection and manufacturing planning. The second agreement covers the plasma volumes under Biotest’s existing contracts with third-party suppliers in Europe. Grifols will provide equivalent volumes for the remaining duration of those contracts.


Settled through the offset of intercompany debt, the acquisition reduces Biotest’s leverage and secures its plasma supply for the next 30 years, while further strengthening its long-term partnership with Grifols. The transaction is expected to close on December 31, 2026, subject to the relevant regulatory approvals.


**Strengthening the security of plasma supply in Europe**


The integration of Biotest’s collection operations is a further step in Grifols’ long-term strategy of helping regions improve and secure their plasma supply. More than 300,000 patients in Europe depend on plasma-derived medicines to treat rare and chronic conditions, many of which have no alternative treatment options. As diagnosis improves, new therapeutic uses emerge and the population ages, demand for these medicines continues to grow.
